navigation.tagline: Certified strength coach. Measure it, plan it, adjust it.

hero.title: Your body follows a plan, not a mood
hero.description: Triple-certified strength coach. I build programs around your real life: your level, your time, your injuries. Then I stay close enough that they actually get done.
hero.imageAlt: Athlete training in a dark gym

credentials.title: Three certifications, one method
credentials.description: Coaching is not a personal opinion. Every call I make in a session rests on training I have done and can account for.

fitness.title: BPJEPS Fitness Activities
fitness.description: The foundation: build a safe session, correct it live, and adapt it to the person in front of me.

science.title: BSc Sport Science, Coaching
science.description: Understanding why a load works, and above all when it stops working.

strength.title: Strength and conditioning
strength.description: Building strength and power without breaking the mechanics. That is where performance is decided.

features.title: Six rules that never move
features.description: They do not depend on your level or your goal. They decide everything else.

assessment.title: Measure before you program
assessment.description: No plan starts from a hunch. The first appointment exists to set a starting point in numbers.

individual.title: One plan per athlete
individual.description: Two people with the same goal do not follow the same program. Their history is not the same.

load.title: Load is steered, not endured
load.description: We push when the indicators allow it and back off the moment they stop allowing it.

progression.title: Progress gets proven
progression.description: Same tests, same conditions, every six weeks. Numbers settle it, not impressions.

longevity.title: Last before you shine
longevity.description: An injury costs more time than any strength block will ever win back.

technique.title: Technique before load
technique.description: Adding weight to a badly placed movement only makes the problem worse. Fix it first, then load it.

programs.title: Three ways to work together
programs.description: All of them start with the same free assessment. The format gets chosen afterwards, once we know where you stand.

included.report: Written review at the end of each block

milestones.title: How I got here
milestones.description: Nothing spectacular, just a run of decisions that all pointed the same way.

sport.title: Sport first
sport.description: Ten years competing in a club. That is where I learned what a body absorbs over a season, and when it gives out.

fitness.title: The first qualification
fitness.description: BPJEPS Fitness Activities. I stop advising on instinct and start coaching properly.

science.title: The theory behind it
science.description: Sport science degree. Physiology and planning: I finally understand why some things worked and others did not.

analysis.title: A hobby on the side
analysis.description: I start analysing football matches for fun, camera and notebook. A pastime that taught me to read a movement in detail.

strength.title: The specialism
strength.description: Strength and conditioning certification. Strength, power and endurance stop being three separate subjects.

studio.title: Coaching full time
studio.description: This becomes my main job. Beginners, seasoned athletes, people coming back from injury: the method applies to all of them.

milestones.imageAlt: Max Jobert in his training gym

assessment.question: Is the assessment really free?
assessment.answer: Yes. One hour, no commitment and no card details. You leave with your measurements and your three priorities, even if we do not work together afterwards.

level.question: Do I need to be fit already?
level.answer: No. I coach competitors and people who have not trained in ten years alike. The plan starts where you are, not at an assumed level.

place.question: Where do sessions happen?
place.answer: In a gym or outdoors depending on what the day calls for. The venue gets set at the assessment, around what you have access to.

rhythm.question: How often should I train?
rhythm.answer: Two to four sessions a week depending on the format. We start from the time you actually have, not the time you wish you had.

nutrition.question: Do you cover nutrition too?
nutrition.answer: I give simple guidance that fits your plan. For proper dietary follow-up I point you to a professional who does that for a living.

cancel.question: Can I stop partway through?
cancel.answer: Yes. Sessions can be cancelled up to twenty-four hours ahead, and no format commits you beyond the block under way.

outcomes.title: What you actually came for
outcomes.description: Three reasons come up almost every time. The plan changes, the way it gets built does not.

strength.title: Get stronger
strength.description: Build muscle and strength without paying for it with your joints. We progress in blocks, measure, and adjust.

conditioning.title: Last longer
conditioning.description: Get your breath and your energy back. Conditioning is dosed like strength, not run to exhaustion.

technique.title: Move properly
technique.description: Fix the movements that hurt or hold you back. That is usually what unlocks everything else.
